recipes.name: Blue Cucumber Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 large cucumbers, peeled and sliced in half lengthwise
1 pinch white pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Scoop out cucumber seeds using a spoon; slice into thick half-moons, then place on a paper towel-lined plate. Sprinkle with ½ teaspoon salt; set aside.

Combine sour cream, onion, white wine vinegar, dill, sugar, and white pepper in a large bowl; fold in blue cheese until incorporated. Pat cucumber slices dry with paper towels; gently stir into blue cheese mixture until evenly coated.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour; season with salt just before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Blue Cucumber Salad
raw_recipe.description: For this blue cucumber salad recipe, peeled and seeded cucumber half moons are combined with sour cream, dill, and tangy blue cheese for loads of flavor.

review.reviewBody: I made this to go with some buffalo hot wings... it was perfect! The sour cream and blue cheese with the crisp coolness of cucumbers went perfectly. We thought this was much better than simply using a blue cheese dipping sauce. I didn't change anything from the recipe, but I have to admit I don't usually measure these types of recipes. Thanks for a great new way to accompany wings!

This was so delish!!! Was a splendid addition to dinner this evening! I used dried dill instead of fresh & I didn’t deseed & cut cucumber rounds into halves. I also cut my onions slightly differently too; I didn’t dice them into small pieces. I also added extra bleu cheese & added tomatoes. The dressing is so delicious, I absolutely love this dish & will be making again very soon!!

I love cukes and blue cheese, but had never had this type of salad before. That has changed forever. It was a crowd pleaser at our Thanksgiving table and is going to be a recipe I make frequently throughout the year as well. I used English cukes which have no seeds. I did peel them, but I am sure that is not needed. I replaced the onion with shallots and having no white pepper, just used black. Only a purist would tell and then it would be difficult due to the dill. I made it the day before so it had ample time for the flavors to marry. Excellent salad and one you should try soon. This was just one of four, five star dishes on our Thanksgiving table this year. Thank you Allrecipes.com and all those who contribute. I am a devoted fan.
Fan-freaking-tastic! I followed the recipe exactly, but also added cherry tomatoes, avocado chunks and fresh chives. This is going to be a daily lunch while the cukes and tomatoes are coming in.

We're really not big cucumber fans, but we do love blue cheese. This is a fantastic recipe for anyone who likes blue cheese. The dill is a nice touch as well. We didn't use sugar and it was not missed. I have never salted cucumber to draw out moisture before and I think it was absolutely necessary to help the sour cream to not go watery. I'm glad this was included in the directions. Thanks for a keeper madermouse.

I had a huge almost two foot cucumber that was a gift and I was unsure what to do with it. This recipe was perfect. My only issue was that the salad still got watery and I don't think the cucumbers sat long enough. When I make this again, I will let them sit longer. Very nice and delicious salad! Thanks!

This is great. It's sweet and salty , creamy and crunchy. I used plain yogurt instead of sour cream as that is what I had on hand. I think this would be nice with feta cheese too but really liked the blue cheese.
Fabulous salad!!!! Who would have thought blue cheese and cucumbers together. I will definitely make this again.
Love this! Complete hit at a recent family pot luck.
Excellent, but you have to like blue cheese.
I just didn't care for the flavor combination. I will save the blue cheese for other salads and leave it out of the cucumber salad.
Had to add a lot of extra vinegar, salt, and sour cream to make it taste right but it turned out very good.

This was delicious! I love blue cheese, and just the addition of it takes the standard cucumber salad to a whole new level. I would never have thought to add it to a salad like this, but it really works here. The onions also add a nice sweetness. Thanks madermouse for the great recipe and for the info on the sour cream as well!
If you love blue cheese, you'll love this dish. Lindsay recommended this recipe on the Buzz, so I knew it had to be good.
